content:
Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I have more than five years of experience across machine learning and NLP, including building and operating production systems for document classification and working with customer-support complaint data. I am especially interested in applying that experience to AI tools that help merchants get answers quickly and support teams route and handle requests effectively.

At Slavonica Document AI, I developed and shipped a document-classification system for OCR-processed invoices, contracts and decisions. It reaches 94% accuracy and a 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes, processing approximately 15,000 documents per day. I fine-tuned transformer models with PyTorch and Hugging Face, deployed them as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure, and used MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry. I also implemented production-quality monitoring; when an OCR change reduced accuracy by nine percentage points, monitoring helped identify the issue and support remediation within a week.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying customer complaints into 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer-service management. I have also built a weekend RAG question-answering prototype over Croatian laws, which gave me hands-on experience with the basic retrieval-augmented approach; it was a prototype, not a production system. Alongside this work, my PhD research focuses on Croatian-language processing, including named entity recognition, and I have built an annotated dataset of 4,000 legal and administrative documents.

Quillstone’s focus on customer-support automation and its emphasis on ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes appeal to me. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my production ML, text-processing and monitoring experience to the team and contribute to practical AI systems for merchant support.

Kind regards,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, credible and well-tailored cover letter. It clearly connects Petra’s production document-classification work, customer complaint classification, RAG prototype and NLP research to customer-support AI. The use of concrete metrics—94% accuracy, 0.91 macro F1, 15,000 documents per day, 11 complaint topics and a nine-percentage-point incident—gives the letter strong evidence and impact. The explicit statement that the RAG project was a weekend prototype and not a production system is appropriately transparent. The tone is professional and the letter is concise. The main content limitation is that it does not mention the computer science degree, strong Python capability or Azure/MLflow in terms that fully mirror the job requirements; these are present in the associated CV but could be reinforced briefly in the letter. The final paragraph is also somewhat generic compared with the highly specific middle paragraphs.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard headings-free letter structure, readable paragraphs, common job-related terms and no problematic tables, graphics or unusual formatting. It includes important keywords such as machine learning, NLP, production systems, customer-support complaint data, RAG, PyTorch, Hugging Face, FastAPI, Docker, Azure, MLflow, model monitoring and named entity recognition. AI screening probability is high when assessed together with the associated CV, because the strongest technical keywords and evidence are present across the application. For the cover letter alone, screening coverage is slightly weaker because Python, computer science degree, MLOps and model serving are not all named directly in the letter. The document appropriately avoids unsupported claims about production RAG, AWS, Kubernetes or LLM fine-tuning.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The application aligns well with the role’s core focus on building and operating language-focused ML systems for customer support. Production model serving, monitoring, Azure deployment, MLflow, transformer fine-tuning, text classification and customer complaint data are directly relevant. The RAG prototype provides truthful exposure to an AI-product pattern, although it is not equivalent to production experience. The letter also aligns with Quillstone’s interest in practical customer-support automation and references ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes without making unsupported claims. The candidate meets the degree requirement through an MSc in Computer Science, has more than four years of relevant experience overall, has strong Python and Azure experience, and shows MLflow-based MLOps experience. The material does not explicitly establish data versioning, orchestration beyond MLflow, feature engineering or data-ingestion pipeline experience; these are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the opening paragraph after the sentence beginning “I have more than five years,” add the verified qualification and strongest language keyword: “I hold an MSc in Computer Science and bring strong Python experience across NLP, model development and production ML systems.” This makes the degree and Python requirements visible in the cover letter without adding unsupported claims.
2. In the second paragraph, change “deployed them as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure, and used MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry” to “served them as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure and used MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry and production MLOps.” This more directly reflects the advertisement’s terminology while remaining supported by the candidate’s CV.
3. In the third paragraph, revise the RAG sentence to make the relevant capability explicit while retaining the important limitation: “I also built a weekend RAG question-answering prototype over Croatian laws, using sentence-transformers, FAISS and an open-weight LLM through an API; it was a prototype rather than a production system.” This gives ATS and human reviewers clearer evidence of the specific tools and RAG experience.
4. In the final paragraph, replace the generic sentence “I would welcome the opportunity to bring my production ML, text-processing and monitoring experience to the team” with “I would welcome the opportunity to bring my Python-based production ML, model-serving, monitoring and text-processing experience to systems that answer merchant questions and route support requests.” This better mirrors the role’s responsibilities without claiming prior experience with merchant-support assistants or ticket-routing systems.

Dear Quillstone Payments Hiring Team,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role. I have more than five years of experience across machine learning and NLP, including building and operating production systems for document classification and working with customer-support complaint data. I hold an MSc in Computer Science and bring strong Python experience across NLP, model development and production ML systems. I am especially interested in applying that experience to AI tools that help merchants get answers quickly and support teams route and handle requests effectively.

At Slavonica Document AI, I developed and shipped a document-classification system for OCR-processed invoices, contracts and decisions. It reaches 94% accuracy and a 0.91 macro F1 across 23 classes, processing approximately 15,000 documents per day. I fine-tuned transformer models with PyTorch and Hugging Face, served them as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure and used MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry and production MLOps. I also implemented production-quality monitoring; when an OCR change reduced accuracy by nine percentage points, monitoring helped identify the issue and support remediation within a week.

My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying customer complaints into 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer-service management. I also built a weekend RAG question-answering prototype over Croatian laws, using sentence-transformers, FAISS and an open-weight LLM through an API; it was a prototype rather than a production system. Alongside this work, my PhD research focuses on Croatian-language processing, including named entity recognition, and I have built an annotated dataset of 4,000 legal and administrative documents.

Quillstone’s focus on customer-support automation and its emphasis on ownership, teamwork and learning from mistakes appeal to me. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my Python-based production ML, model-serving, monitoring and text-processing experience to systems that answer merchant questions and route support requests.

Kind regards,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional cover letter with a clear progression from production document classification to customer-complaint NLP and a truthful RAG prototype. It uses measurable outcomes effectively, including 94% accuracy, 0.91 macro F1, 15,000 documents per day, and the nine-percentage-point monitoring incident. The letter is concise, readable, and appropriately transparent that the RAG work was a prototype rather than a production system. The motivation is relevant to customer-support automation, though the closing could connect the candidate's experience slightly more directly to Quillstone's specific use cases: answering merchant questions, routing tickets, and supporting agents.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly in plain text with standard paragraphs, an exact target job title, and relevant keywords including Python, NLP, production ML systems, model serving, FastAPI, Docker, Azure, MLflow, monitoring, transformers, customer complaints, and RAG. It would benefit from using the more specific supported Azure terms from the candidate material—Azure ML and Azure App Service—and from naming the MLflow model registry explicitly. The letter does not contain unsupported tools or achievements. AI screening probability is strong for the core NLP, RAG, Python, Azure, model-serving, and monitoring criteria, but lower for data versioning, feature engineering, and data-ingestion pipelines because the candidate material does not establish those areas.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's focus on production ML, text processing, customer-support data, model serving, monitoring, Azure, Python, and RAG. The complaint-topic classification experience is particularly relevant to ticket routing and support operations, while the production document-classification system demonstrates operational ownership and measurable scale. The letter also references Quillstone's ownership, teamwork, and learning-from-mistakes culture without overclaiming cultural fit. The candidate has a computer science degree and the document shows experience shipping a production ML system, but the material does not clearly establish at least four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production. The candidate material also does not demonstrate data versioning, feature engineering, or data-ingestion pipelines as defined in the advertisement; these are requirement gaps rather than cover-letter defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS/alignment enhancement: In the second paragraph, change "served them as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure and used MLflow for experiment tracking, model registry and production MLOps" to "served them as FastAPI services in Docker on Azure App Service, used Azure ML and MLflow for experiment tracking and model registry, and implemented production model-quality monitoring." This uses the candidate's exact supported platform names and strengthens alignment with the ad's model-serving, cloud, and MLOps terminology.

MINOR relevance enhancement: In the third paragraph, change "My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included classifying customer complaints into 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer-service management" to "My earlier work at Baranjska kreditna banka included customer-complaint topic classification into 11 topics for weekly reporting to customer-service management, directly relevant to support-request routing and analysis." Keep the added connection limited to relevance; do not imply that the system was an automated ticket-routing product.
